conviction_note: A first-of-its-kind scheduled Q3 Trading Update on a 15-analyst FTSE 100 name with FY26 guidance already raised at the half (EPS above the top of 6-9%), so the release most likely reiterates; abs_move 2.3 is the European 'guide reiterated' base, and p_up 45 leans slightly down because the stock goes in at a multi-year high after a +5.4% 20-day run, PRT volumes are tracking below last year's £11bn-by-October pace in a soft, competitive market, and three of its last four results-type releases fell (Q3/Retail update Oct 2025 -1.57%); the findings sum (-0.7) and the scaled number (-0.23) agree in sign, the sum is larger because each small negative is sized alone while p_up carries the uncertainty once.

FY26 EPS 'above the top end of 6-9%' reiterated; a further raise is possible but unsourced; no change expected

session_check: bmo — the issuer's HY26 financial calendar lists 'Q3 Trading Update 16 November 2026', and L&G's results-type RNS release at 07:00 London (HY26 05 Aug 2026 07:00; FY25 11 Mar 2026 07:00; Oct 2025 current-trading/Retail deep dive 07:00), https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/LGEN; the 16 Nov release itself is not yet out, so this is the issuer's pattern, not its timestamp
positioning_check: FCA aggregated net short 4.72% as of 2026-11-11, previous 4.74% (-0.02 pts): large for a FTSE 100 insurer but flat, neither building nor covering into the print (https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv, per sealed baseline). Per-holder split not retrieved.

findings.finding: PRT volumes are tracking below last year's pace: £5.7bn global PRT written or exclusive at end-July 2026 against £11bn YTD at 23 Oct 2025, in a UK bulk-annuity market XPS put below £10bn for H1 with strong insurer pricing competition; even with the £1.7bn UBS buy-in the Q3 YTD figure likely prints under the prior-year comparator.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Oct 2025 update with £11bn PRT and top-end EPS guidance fell 1.3-1.6%; HY26 with 'strict pricing discipline' on £5.7bn rose 0.79%, so the market has already absorbed lower volume once.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the company told the market about pricing discipline at HY and the stock rose. What is not yet known is the Q3 number against the £11bn comparator; if the market had priced a weak volume print it would not be at a multi-year high, +5.4% over 20 days, above most published targets.
findings.independence: XPS Q3 2026 trustee update (22 Jul 2026): H1 market below £10bn, fewer £bn+ deals, pricing strong — https://www.xpsgroup.com/news-views/insights-briefings/bulk-annuity-market-q3-2026-trustee-update/ ; prior-year comparator https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/lg-track-post-top-end-eps-growth-sets-out-retail-ambitions

findings.finding: L&G has sold most of its own results-type releases: Oct 2025 current-trading update -1.57% despite top-end guidance, HY25 -2.03%, FY25 -6.77%, HY26 +0.79% — three of four down over this stage's window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As stated: 3 of 4 results-type releases negative, median about -1.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: A reaction pattern rather than a fact about the print; it sits against a stock running into the date (+3.35% over 5 days, +0.67% on the session Aviva rallied), which is what a market expecting a sell-the-news print would not be doing.
findings.independence: Price series https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/LGEN.L?range=2y&interval=1d (2025-10-23 -1.57%); AJ Bell 23 Oct 2025 reports -1.3% intraday https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/lg-track-post-top-end-eps-growth-sets-out-retail-ambitions

findings.finding: Peer read-through: Aviva's Q3 2026 trading update on 13 Nov ('strong performance demonstrates benefits of diversified model', on track for three-year group targets) sent Aviva +2.7% on the day; M&G's 5 Nov Q3 (BPA £1.8bn YTD, FY >£2.5bn) was flat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured L&G reaction to peer Q3 updates.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: both peer prints sit before the window opens at the 13 Nov close, and L&G rose 0.67% with Aviva on the day. Aviva is general-insurance-led, so the read across to a PRT/asset-management group is weak.

findings.finding: Solvency II coverage has been falling — 232% to 210% at FY25 (reported as a miss, the day the stock fell 6.77%) and 201% at HY26 — while the £1.2bn buyback runs, so the Q3 ratio is a live line with no sourced bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY25 (solvency 210% missed predictions) -6.77%; HY26 (201%, still above the 160-190% range) +0.79%.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction of the Q3 ratio is genuinely unknown (it depends on Q3 gilt yields and spreads, which I did not measure), so this is sized as a small skew from the trend, not as a call.

findings.finding: M&G's Q3 2026 asset-management net flows halved year on year (£0.7bn against £1.5bn), a weak read-across for L&G Asset Management's Q3 flows after a record H1 ANNR.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HY26's record ANNR and +37% fee-related earnings came with +0.79%.
findings.why_not_priced: A proxy only: M&G's institutional and wholesale mix differs from L&G's index/LDI-heavy book, and nothing from L&G or a direct counterparty corroborates it.

outside_window.finding: Bid speculation: FT (14 May 2026) reported insurers and alternative asset managers circling L&G, shares +5%; the CEO denied considering a sale or break-up. No offer period, no Rule 2.4 announcement on RNS. It supports the premium to sell-side targets; it resolves only if a bidder appears, which is not dated.
Non-Executive Director Carolyn Johnson retires from the Board effective 1 January 2027; no price relevance.
